LONDON — On Thursday evening, 17 September, the historic setting of 1 Belgrave Square became a meeting point for fashion, culture and diplomacy as more than 200 guests gathered for the private preview of “Diplomacy in Fashion: The London Chapter.” The exhibition brings together 21 contemporary Romanian designers in a celebration of creativity and cultural exchange during London Fashion Week. The evening was hosted by H.E. Laura Popescu, Ambassador of Romania to the United Kingdom ; H.E. Giles Portman, British Ambassador to Romania ; Aura Woodward, Director of the Romanian Cultural Institute in London; and Lucie Portman, curator of the project. Produced by Modern Owners under the concept “The Manifest: Romanian couture, unpacked in London,” the exhibition presents Romanian fashion in a setting where heritage and contemporary design meet. As the first major fashion exhibition hosted by the Romanian Cultural Institute in London, it offers a platform for Romanian designers to engage with an international audience and expand their presence beyond Romania. The exhibition’s scenography follows a symbolic journey of creative mobility — from cargo crates in the arrival area to designer pieces displayed within the historic salons of 1 Belgrave Square. It is a visual narrative about movement, discovery and the ways in which fashion can travel across borders, connecting people through design. A gathering of creative talent Among the designers attending the opening were Andreea Raicu, Kati Szalai, Alina Pușcaș, Corina Boboc, Alina Lazariu, Ramona Nacu, Sabina Georgescu a nd Marius Mușat, alongside supporters who had travelled from Bucharest especially for the occasion. The guest list reflected the event’s broad cultural and professional reach. Attendees included David Leigh-Pemberton, Deputy Director of Policy and Engagement at the British Fashion Council; Sir George Iacobescu, CEO of Canary Wharf Group; pianist Alexandra Dariescu, following her recent debut at the BBC Proms; and photographer Alexandra Drăgoi, whose work includes the official portrait of British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and collaborations with Downing Street. For the Romanian Cultural Institute in London, the exhibition marks a new chapter in presenting Romanian fashion to international audiences. “Diplomacy is often defined as the art of the possible. I like to define cultural diplomacy as the art of bringing people together,” said Aura Woodward, Director of ICR London. She added that the exhibition provides a platform for Romanian designers to collaborate, build bridges and expand their international presence. Fashion as a language of connection For H.E. Laura Popescu , fashion is also a way to express cultural identity and share Romanian creativity with the world. “I am always proud to wear pieces by Romanian designers and to show what fashion from Romania can create. Diplomacy in Fashion builds authentic bridges between our countries through creativity and culture,” she said. H.E. Giles Portman placed the event within the wider context of Romanian-British relations. Following the connection of Romanian-British partnerships in investment and technology at Cambridge Tech Week, he noted, the evening brought design and fashion to London. “This week we connected Romanian-British partnerships in investment and technology at Cambridge Tech Week, and tonight we are bringing design and fashion to London,” he said. “We wanted to transfer the energy from Bucharest directly to Belgrave Square. ” He described the bilateral relationship as vibrant, adding that creativity opens real human and economic connections. For curator Lucie Portman, bringing Romanian designers to London was a natural continuation of her experiences in Romania. “Romania won us over from the very first moment through its nature, culture and the talent of its people. Following the events in Bucharest, the natural next step was to bring the creations of Romanian designers to London,” she said. The project, she explained, brings together passion and diplomacy to create direct connections between designers and international audiences. The dialogue also extends to architecture. Cosmin Popescu of One United Properties observed that, much like architecture, fashion communicates values long before a conversation begins. Cities, he noted, thrive through harmonious buildings and open spaces, and the company supports projects that create context and bring people together. Open to the public Following the private preview, “Diplomacy in Fashion: The London Chapter” is open to the public at the Romanian Cultural Institute in London from 18 to 20 September 2026 , daily from 10:00 to 17:00 . Admission is free. The event is held under the patronage of the Embassy of Romania in London, the Embassy of the United Kingdom in Bucharest and the Romanian Cultural Institute in London. Congratulations to All Designers Featured in the Exhibition! Nine O’Clock congratulates all the designers featured in “Diplomacy in Fashion: The London Chapter” for bringing Romanian creativity, craftsmanship and contemporary design to the international stage. The event took place at the Embassy of the Hellenic Republic in Bucharest on Tuesday, 11 November 2025, starting at 3:00 PM. It also marked the launch of the book “Top Interviews, Messages & Speeches from Ambassadors and CEOs – Second Edition, 2025” , a volume gathering strategic perspectives from global leaders.
